coverage.feedback: The accepted cases break down compound requirements into individual test cases unnecessarily, resulting in overgeneration and redundancy. Specifically, requirements R-002, R-003, R-009, R-010, R-014, R-016, and R-018 are split into multiple separate test cases (e.g., separating add/delete or sort/reverse-sort), whereas the rejected candidates properly group these related actions into single comprehensive test cases corresponding directly to each requirement. No coverage gaps are present, but the accepted cases exhibit excess test case proliferation by atomizing actions that belong to a single requirement.

output.feedback: All test cases map one-to-one to the provided requirements, accurately capturing the specified behaviors including additions, deletions, modifications, view behaviors, and restrictions. No redundancy, missing coverage, or blockers were identified.
All requirements and test cases align correctly with the functional specifications.

The accepted cases break down compound requirements into individual test cases unnecessarily, resulting in overgeneration and redundancy. Specifically, requirements R-002, R-003, R-009, R-010, R-014, R-016, and R-018 are split into multiple separate test cases (e.g., separating add/delete or sort/reverse-sort), whereas the rejected candidates properly group these related actions into single comprehensive test cases corresponding directly to each requirement. No coverage gaps are present, but the accepted cases exhibit excess test case proliferation by atomizing actions that belong to a single requirement.
